query: Starting from a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies, what single intervention could overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness while retaining or increasing strength? The hypothesis should address the tendency for dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries to produce local stress concentrations, microcracking, and catastrophic damage during straining. Specify the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted strength and ductility relative to the untreated starting material, the applicable testing and operating conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled post-solidification aging treatment that induces the precipitation of coherent nano-scale particles specifically at the lamellar colony boundaries in the eutectic HEA will reduce dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations, thereby overcoming tensile brittleness while retaining or increasing strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure composed of dual-phase lamellar colonies that exhibit limited room-temperature tensile ductility due to dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
generation.intervention: Apply a post-solidification aging heat treatment (in an inert atmosphere) at an optimized sub-solvus temperature and time to induce fine, coherent precipitates selectively at the lamellar interfaces.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature tensile testing; aging treatment performed under inert atmosphere; subsequent microstructural characterization (TEM/SEM) to verify the formation and distribution of nano-scale precipitates at internal boundaries.
generation.structural_mediator: Nano-scale, coherent precipitates precipitated at the lamellar colony boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The precipitates act as interfacial reinforcements that disrupt the continuous internal boundaries, reduce the effective length for dislocation pile-ups, and promote more uniform dislocation transmission across colonies. This reduces local stress concentrations that typically lead to microcracking and catastrophic damage under tension while maintaining or enhancing the overall load-bearing capacity.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in room-temperature tensile ductility (i.e. higher strain-to-failure) while retaining or positively influencing the strength of the eutectic HEA compared to the untreated state.
generation.baseline: Untreated eutectic HEA with dual-phase lamellar colonies, which exhibits limited tensile ductility and brittleness due to dislocation accumulation at internal boundaries.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected to be sensitive to the precise aging temperature and duration; over-aging might lead to coarser precipitates or excessive interfacial strengthening that could reintroduce brittleness. The outcome may also depend on subtle compositional variations within the eutectic HEA.
generation.uncertainty: While the mechanism of precipitate-induced dislocation interruption is well established in similar multi-phase alloys, the optimal processing window to achieve the desired nanoscale precipitate morphology in this specific eutectic HEA is not yet defined. There is uncertainty regarding the extent of ductility improvement achievable without detrimental over-aging effects.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of specimens from the same batch of the eutectic HEA. Subject one set to the proposed aging treatment (with parameters chosen based on preliminary calibration) and leave the other set untreated. Conduct room-temperature tensile tests and microstructural analyses (using TEM/SEM) on both sets.
measurements: Tensile strength and strain-to-failure from tensile tests
Presence, size, and distribution of precipitates at lamellar boundaries
Comparison of stress–strain curves between aged and untreated samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvement in tensile ductility (higher strain-to-failure) while maintaining or enhancing strength compared to the untreated samples, or if the targeted nano-scale precipitates are not observed at the internal lamellar boundaries, then the hypothesis is falsified.

System: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy matrix with in-situ formed TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles.
